doc.title: Jonathan Scales interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 23, 2025

title: Inspiration from outside music
summary: Scales cites John Cage and real life as inspiration; Rowe quotes Maria Schneider on needing to live.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Are you inspired by other artistic genres other than music?

Oh yes. Man, honestly I’m a big fan of John Cage. You know John Cage the thinker of a composer? The philosopher? I’m a big fan of John Cage so like a lot of my information – or not information, sorry – inspiration is coming from outside of music. Like and what

that is right now I mean I feel a little bit inarticulate about that right now because it’s on the spot. But like yeah, I think that life is very influential. Like my music, a lot of my music, it comes from real life.

Maria Schneider said something that I just found was very illuminating. It was right near the end of our interview, and she just said, “Sometimes I tell my composition students, ‘Listen, you just have to live. You have to live. You have to go out and do different things, not just music things. Go out and live and experience other things or your music will suffer for not doing that.’”
